speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node, which is a significant finding. Have you experienced any difficulty swallowing, changes in your voice, or pain in your abdomen that radiates to your back?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of weight loss, night sweats, and a supraclavicular lymph node, I am concerned about lymphoma. Do you have any itching of the skin, or have you noticed any other swollen lymph nodes in your neck, armpits, or groin?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis
REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis: Slight abdominal distension, dullness in left lower quadrant, splenomegaly without rebound tenderness, massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Lymph_Node_Biopsy: Lymphocytes with high proliferative index positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing CD20 positivity confirms a B-cell lymphoma, likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma given the high proliferative index. I need to stage this accurately to plan treatment, so I will order a PET-CT scan to assess for distant metastases. REQUEST TEST: PET_CT

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal PET-CT is unexpected given the biopsy results, which strongly suggest an aggressive B-cell lymphoma like DLBCL. I will request medical images to visually correlate the lymphadenopathy with the scan findings. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness and splenomegaly suggest significant organ involvement that the PET-CT may have underestimated or missed due to technical factors. I need to rule out bone marrow infiltration to finalize the staging. REQUEST TEST: Bone_Marrow_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the CD20+ B-cell lymphoma with splenomegaly and normal PET/CT and bone marrow, this presentation is highly suggestive of Splenic Marginal Zone Lymphoma or a low-grade B-cell lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Splenic Marginal Zone Lymphoma
